newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Wary France hastens Taiwan's Mirage delivery - report.
newsitem.headline: Wary France hastens Taiwan's Mirage delivery - report.

text.p: France will speed up delivery to Taiwan of an initial batch of Mirage 2000-5 fighter jets, aiming to avert political frictions at a May summit in China, a Taipei newspaper reported on Monday.

By moving delivery forward one month to April, Paris hopes to minimise pressure from China, Taiwan's arch rival, when President Jacques Chirac visits Beijing in May, the Central Daily News quoted unnamed Taiwan air force sources as saying.
The defence ministry declined to comment on the report.

Taiwan ordered 60 of the advanced French warplanes in a 1992 deal that sparked a serious rift in France's ties with China, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.
Beijing downgraded its ties with Paris and laid on economic sanctions -- measures it reversed only after France agreed in 1994 to halt all arms sales to the Nationalist-ruled island.

The newspaper, run by the ruling Nationalist Party, did not say how many of the 60 Mirage fighters would be delivered in the first batch, but said they were expected to be commissioned by the air force in May.
Planemaker Dassault Aviation had sent 12 engineers and senior flight officers to help the air force prepare for the planes' arrival, the report said.
France has shipped engines, electronic systems and other spare parts to Taiwan, it said.
The warplanes will arrive at Hualien port in eastern Taiwan, transferred to the nearby Chiashan air base for inspection and finally deployed at an air base in northern Hsinchu, it said.
In the row over France's Mirage sale to Taiwan, Beijing closed the French consulate in the southern city of Guangzhou and froze French firms out of lucrative Chinese contracts.

China lifted the freeze in 1994 after Paris agreed that the "one China" terms of its diplomatic relations with Beijing obliged France to abandon its policy of arming Taiwan, the last bastion of the exiled Republic of China government.
